questions.question: Write an expression for "5 more than n".
questions.why: 5n means 5 × n, not 5 added to n

questions.question: Find the value of 3x when x = 4.
questions.why: 3x is 3 × x, not the digits 3 and 4 written together

questions.question: Find the value of x² when x = 6.
questions.why: x² is x × x, not x × 2

questions.question: Write "double a number m" as an expression.
questions.why: Write the number before the letter: 2m

questions.question: Find the value of 2x + 7 when x = -3.
Find the value of 3x² when x = -2.
questions.why: 36 is (3x)²; the question is 3x², so only x is squared

questions.question: Find the value of (a + b) ÷ 2 when a = 7 and b = -3.
Find the value of 5 - 2y when y = 4.
Using v = u + at, find v when u = 2, a = 3 and t = 5.
Using s = ut + ½at², find s when u = 0, a = 10 and t = 3.
questions.why: Square t before multiplying: 3² = 9, then ½ × 10 × 9

questions.question: Find the value of x² - 4x when x = -1.
density = mass ÷ volume. A block has mass 240 g and volume 30 cm³. Find its density in g/cm³.
The period of a pendulum is T = 2π√(L ÷ g). Find T when L = 2.45 m and g = 9.8 m/s². Give your answer to 2 decimal places with a unit.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: L ÷ g = 0.25.  1 mark: √0.25 = 0.5.  1 mark: T = 2π × 0.5 = π = 3.14 s with unit.
questions.hint: Work inside the square root first.
questions.why: Square-rooting after multiplying by 2π is the wrong order

questions.question: A rectangle has length 2x + 3 and width x - 1. Write and simplify an expression for its perimeter, then find the perimeter when x = 4.5.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: P = 2(2x + 3) + 2(x - 1).  1 mark: simplify to 6x + 4.  1 mark: substitute x = 4.5 to get 31.
questions.hint: Perimeter uses two lengths and two widths.
questions.why: Perimeter needs both lengths and both widths, so double each

questions.question: Using x = -3, show that 2x² and (2x)² give different values and state which is larger.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: 2x² = 2 × 9 = 18.  1 mark: (2x)² = (-6)² = 36.  1 mark: statement that (2x)² is larger because the 2 is squared as well.
questions.hint: In (2x)² the whole bracket is squared.
questions.why: In (2x)², multiply by 2 first and then square

questions.question: Simplify 4a + 3a.
questions.hint: Same letter, so add the numbers.
questions.why: Adding like terms does not change the power

questions.question: Simplify 5b - 2b.
questions.hint: Same letter, so subtract the numbers.

questions.question: Simplify 3 × 4x.
questions.hint: Multiply the numbers; keep the x.

questions.question: Simplify a × b.
questions.hint: Write letters side by side for multiplication.
questions.why: × is written as ab, not a + b

questions.question: Simplify 3x + 2y + 5x - y.
questions.hint: Collect x terms and y terms separately.
questions.why: x and y are different letters; they cannot be combined into xy

questions.question: Simplify 2x² + 5x².
questions.hint: Same letter and same power, so add the numbers.
questions.why: Adding like terms keeps the power at 2

questions.question: Simplify 3x × 4x.
questions.hint: Multiply the numbers, multiply the letters.

questions.question: Simplify x³ × x⁴.
questions.why: Multiply the bases, add the powers: 3 + 4 = 7

questions.question: Simplify y⁸ ÷ y².
questions.why: Subtract the powers: 8 - 2 = 6, do not divide them

questions.question: Simplify (x²)⁵.
questions.hint: Multiply the powers for a power of a power.

questions.question: Simplify (2x³)².
questions.hint: Square the 2 as well as the x³.

questions.question: Simplify (3a²b)(4ab³).
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: 3 × 4 = 12.  1 mark: a² × a = a³.  1 mark: b × b³ = b⁴.
questions.hint: Deal with numbers, then a, then b.
questions.why: Add the powers for each letter: a has 2 + 1, b has 1 + 3

questions.question: Simplify (6x⁵y²) ÷ (2x²y).
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: 6 ÷ 2 = 3.  1 mark: x⁵ ÷ x² = x³.  1 mark: y² ÷ y = y.
questions.hint: Divide the numbers, subtract each power.

questions.question: Simplify (2x²)³ ÷ 4x⁴.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: (2x²)³ = 8x⁶.  1 mark: 8 ÷ 4 = 2.  1 mark: x⁶ ÷ x⁴ = x².
questions.hint: Expand the power of the bracket first.
questions.why: Divide x⁶ by x⁴ as well: subtract the powers

questions.question: Expand 3(x + 4).
questions.why: The 4 must be multiplied by 3 as well

questions.question: Expand 5(y - 2).
questions.hint: Multiply both terms by 5; keep the minus.

questions.question: Expand (x + 2)(x + 3).
questions.hint: First, Outer, Inner, Last, then collect.
questions.why: The two middle terms 3x and 2x must be included

questions.question: Expand (x + 3)².
questions.why: A perfect square has a middle term: 2 × 3 × x = 6x

questions.question: Expand and simplify (2x + 1)(x - 3).
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: 2x × x = 2x².  1 mark: outer and inner: -6x + x = -5x.  1 mark: 1 × (-3) = -3.
questions.why: Include the inner term 1 × x = x, so -6x + x = -5x

questions.question: A square garden of side (x + 3) m has a square pond of side (x - 1) m cut out of it. Find a simplified expression for the remaining area.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: (x + 3)² = x² + 6x + 9.  1 mark: (x - 1)² = x² - 2x + 1.  1 mark: subtract to get 8x + 8.
questions.hint: Area of a square is side squared; remaining = big minus small.
questions.why: Square each side before subtracting; (x+3) - (x-1) is a length, not an area

questions.question: Factorise 4a + 8b.
questions.why: Take out the highest common factor, 4, not 2

questions.question: Factorise fully 4x² + 6x.
questions.hint: HCF includes a number and an x.
questions.why: Not fully factorised: x is also common

questions.question: Factorise 10ab - 15a.
questions.why: a is also a common factor

questions.question: Factorise x² + 5x + 6.
questions.hint: Two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5.

questions.question: Factorise x² - x - 12.
questions.why: 4 - 3 = +1; the middle term is -1, so the larger number is negative

questions.question: Factorise x² - 25.
questions.why: (x - 5)² gives x² - 10x + 25, which has a middle term

questions.question: Factorise x² - 8x + 16.
questions.why: (x + 4)² expands to +8x; the sign must be negative

questions.question: Factorise fully 2x² + 8x + 6.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: common factor 2 gives 2(x² + 4x + 3).  1 mark: factorise the quadratic to (x + 1)(x + 3).  1 mark: fully factorised form with the 2 kept.
questions.why: Correct but not fully factorised: (2x + 2) still has a common factor of 2

questions.question: Explain whether x² + 4 can be factorised using integers. Then factorise x² - 4.
questions.answer: Cannot (no integer pair with product 4 and sum 0); x² - 4 = (x + 2)(x - 2)
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: states that no two integers have product 4 and sum 0, so x² + 4 does not factorise.  1 mark: recognises x² - 4 as a difference of two squares.  1 mark: (x + 2)(x - 2).
questions.hint: Which pairs multiply to +4? Can any add to 0?

questions.question: Solve x + 7 = 12.
questions.why: Undo the +7 by subtracting, not adding

questions.question: Solve 3(x + 2) = 18.
questions.hint: Expand first, or divide both sides by 3.

questions.question: Solve 2(x - 3) = x + 1.
questions.hint: Expand, then collect x on one side.

questions.question: Solve 3(2x - 1) = 4(x + 2) + 1.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: expand both sides: 6x - 3 = 4x + 9.  1 mark: collect: 2x = 12.  1 mark: x = 6 and verification (33 = 33).
questions.hint: Expand both sides fully before collecting.

questions.question: Solve (x + 1) ÷ 2 + (x - 3) ÷ 4 = 5.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: multiply every term by 4: 2(x + 1) + (x - 3) = 20.  1 mark: simplify: 3x - 1 = 20.  1 mark: x = 7 and verification (4 + 1 = 5).
questions.hint: Multiply every term by the lowest common denominator, 4.
questions.why: Multiply the right-hand side by 4 too: 5 × 4 = 20

questions.question: A triangle has sides x + 2, 2x - 1 and 3x + 5 cm. Its perimeter is 36 cm. Find the length of the longest side.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: 6x + 6 = 36.  1 mark: x = 5.  1 mark: sides 7, 9, 20; longest is 20 cm with unit.
questions.hint: Add the three sides and set equal to 36.
questions.why: x = 5 is correct but the question asks for the longest side

questions.question: List the integers that satisfy 1 < x ≤ 4.
questions.why: 1 < x means x is greater than 1, so 1 is not included

questions.question: Is 5 a solution of x ≥ 5? Answer yes or no.
questions.why: ≥ means greater than or equal to, so 5 is included

questions.question: Write "x is less than 3" using a symbol.
questions.hint: Less than points to the smaller value.

questions.question: What is the largest integer that satisfies x < 7?
Solve x + 3 > 8.
questions.why: Keep the inequality sign in the answer

questions.question: Solve -3 < 2x + 1 ≤ 7.
questions.hint: Do the same to all three parts.
questions.why: Subtract 1 from all three parts first, then divide by 2

questions.question: List the integers that satisfy -1 ≤ x - 2 < 2.
Solve 5 - 3x ≥ 11.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: -3x ≥ 6.  1 mark: divide by -3 and reverse the sign: x ≤ -2.  1 mark: verification with a value such as x = -3.
questions.hint: Dividing by a negative reverses the sign.
questions.why: Dividing both sides by -3 reverses the inequality

questions.question: Find the smallest integer n such that 4n + 7 > 50.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: 4n > 43.  1 mark: n > 10.75.  1 mark: smallest integer is 11, with a check that n = 10 fails.
questions.hint: Solve, then round up to the next integer.
questions.why: n = 10 gives 47, which is not greater than 50

questions.question: A taxi charges a fixed fee of 3 plus 1.20 per kilometre. The budget is at most 15. Form an inequality for the distance d and find the maximum whole number of kilometres.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: 3 + 1.2d ≤ 15.  1 mark: d ≤ 10.  1 mark: maximum whole number 10 km stated with unit.
questions.why: Subtract the fixed fee before dividing: 12 ÷ 1.2 = 10

questions.question: A rectangle has sides x and x + 3. Write a simplified expression for its perimeter.
A number n is doubled and then 5 is added. Write the expression.
questions.why: "Doubled then add 5" is 2n + 5; 2(n + 5) doubles after adding

questions.question: Tickets cost 8 each. Write an expression for the cost of t tickets.
questions.hint: Cost per ticket × number of tickets.

questions.question: Ana is a years old. Her brother is 3 years older. Write an expression for her brother's age.
I think of a number, multiply it by 3 and subtract 4. The result is 17. Find the number.
A rectangle with sides x and x + 3 has perimeter 30. Find x.
questions.why: Use the perimeter expression 4x + 6, not x + (x + 3)

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are x, 2x and 3x. Find x.
questions.hint: Angles in a triangle add to 180°.

questions.question: A phone plan costs 10 per month plus 0.05 per minute. Write an expression for the monthly cost of m minutes.
questions.why: The 10 is a fixed amount, not multiplied by m

questions.question: A ride-hailing service charges a fixed fee of 4 plus 1.50 per km. A journey cost 19. Define a variable, form an equation and find the distance.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: defines d = distance in km.  1 mark: 4 + 1.5d = 19.  1 mark: d = 10 km with unit and verification.
questions.why: Subtract the fixed fee 4 before dividing by 1.5

questions.question: A tank holds 500 litres and drains at 20 litres per minute. Write a formula for the volume V after t minutes and find when the tank is empty.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: V = 500 - 20t.  1 mark: sets V = 0.  1 mark: t = 25 minutes with unit.
questions.why: Draining reduces the volume, so subtract

questions.question: Two consecutive integers add to 61. Define a variable and find them.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: let n = smaller integer, next is n + 1.  1 mark: 2n + 1 = 61.  1 mark: n = 30, so 30 and 31.
questions.why: Two consecutive integers are n and n + 1; their sum is 2n + 1

questions.question: A car rental costs 40 per day plus 0.25 per kilometre. A 3-day rental cost 215. How many kilometres were driven?
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: 3 × 40 = 120 fixed.  1 mark: 120 + 0.25k = 215.  1 mark: k = 380 km with unit.
questions.hint: Work out the fixed part for 3 days first.
questions.why: Subtract the daily charges (120), then divide by 0.25

questions.question: Gym A charges a joining fee of 30 plus 12 per month. Gym B charges 15 per month with no joining fee. Define a variable, write an expression for each gym, find when the costs are equal, interpret the result and state one limitation of the model.
questions.answer: Equal after 10 months; A cheaper beyond 10 months
questions.markScheme: Strand i (1 mark): m = number of months; A = 30 + 12m, B = 15m.  Strand ii-iii (2 marks): 30 + 12m = 15m, m = 10.  Strand v (1 mark): costs equal at 10 months; B is cheaper for a shorter membership, A for longer.  Strand iv-v (1 mark): limitation, e.g. prices may change, no discounts, membership may not be whole months.
questions.hint: Set the two expressions equal to each other.

questions.question: A spring is 12 cm long with nothing attached and extends 2.5 cm for every 100 g added. Write a model for the length L (cm) in terms of mass m (g). Find the mass that makes the spring 20 cm long. State when the model stops being valid.
questions.markScheme: Strand i (1 mark): L = 12 + 0.025m.  Strand ii-iii (2 marks): 12 + 0.025m = 20, m = 320 g.  Strand iv (1 mark): accuracy depends on the 2.5 cm per 100 g being exact.  Strand v (1 mark): beyond the elastic limit the spring deforms and the linear model no longer holds.
questions.hint: 2.5 cm per 100 g is 0.025 cm per gram.

questions.question: A phone battery starts at 100% and loses 8% per hour of video. Write a model for the charge C after h hours, find when it reaches 20%, and comment on the accuracy of the model.
questions.markScheme: Strand i (1 mark): C = 100 - 8h.  Strand ii-iii (2 marks): 100 - 8h = 20, h = 10 hours.  Strand iv (1 mark): drain is rarely constant (screen brightness, background apps), so 10 hours is an estimate.  Strand v (1 mark): the answer is plausible for video playback; negative C would be meaningless beyond 12.5 hours.
questions.why: 12.5 hours is when the battery reaches 0%, not 20%

questions.question: Make x the subject of y = x + 5.
Make x the subject of y = 4x.
Make a the subject of P = 2a.
Make x the subject of y = x - 7.
Make x the subject of y = 3x + 2.
questions.why: Subtract 2 from y before dividing by 3

questions.question: Make a the subject of v = u + at.
questions.hint: Subtract u, then divide by t.
questions.why: Divide the whole of (v - u) by t

questions.question: Make w the subject of A = lw.
Make x the subject of y = x ÷ 4 - 1.
Make r the subject of A = πr².
questions.hint: Divide by π, then square root.
questions.why: The square root covers the whole of A ÷ π

questions.question: Make t the subject of v = u + at.
questions.hint: Subtract u, then divide by a.
questions.why: Divide the whole of (v - u) by a

questions.question: Make r the subject of C = 2πr.
Make x the subject of y = 2(x + 3).
Make s the subject of v² = u² + 2as.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: v² - u² = 2as.  1 mark: divide by 2a.  1 mark: final form with brackets correct.
questions.why: The whole of (v² - u²) is divided by 2a; brackets are needed

questions.question: Make r the subject of V = πr²h.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: divide by πh: r² = V ÷ (πh).  1 mark: square root both sides.  1 mark: root covers the whole fraction.
questions.hint: Divide by everything multiplying r² first.
questions.why: The square root must cover V ÷ (πh), not V alone

questions.question: Make L the subject of T = 2π√(L ÷ g).
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: divide by 2π.  1 mark: square both sides: T² ÷ (4π²) = L ÷ g.  1 mark: multiply by g.
questions.hint: Isolate the square root, then square both sides.

questions.question: Describe the term-to-term rule of 2, 6, 18, 54, ...
questions.hint: Each term is three times the previous.
questions.why: 2 to 6 is +4 but 6 to 18 is +12; the rule is × 3

questions.question: Find the 5th term of 4, 7, 10, 13, ...
questions.hint: Add the common difference once more.

questions.question: Find the nth term of 3, 5, 7, 9, ...
questions.why: The difference tells you the coefficient of n: 2n

questions.question: Find the 10th term of the sequence with nth term 5n - 2.
Write the first three terms of the sequence with nth term 4n + 3.
questions.why: n starts at 1, so the first term is 4 + 3 = 7

questions.question: Find the nth term of 5, 9, 13, 17, ...
questions.hint: d = 4, first term 5, so a - d = 1.
questions.why: Subtract d from the first term: 5 - 4 = 1

questions.question: Find the nth term of 10, 8, 6, 4, ...
questions.why: A decreasing sequence has a negative coefficient of n

questions.question: Is 101 a term of the sequence with nth term 4n + 1? If so, which term?
questions.why: 4n = 100 gives n = 25, a whole number, so yes

questions.question: Find the nth term of 7, 12, 17, 22, ...
questions.why: Subtract d from the first term: 7 - 5 = 2

questions.question: Is 90 a term of the sequence with nth term 3n + 2? Justify your answer.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: sets 3n + 2 = 90.  1 mark: 3n = 88, n = 29.33.  1 mark: n is not a positive integer, so 90 is not a term.
questions.hint: Solve for n and check whether it is a whole number.
questions.why: n = 29.33 is not a whole number, so 90 is not in the sequence

questions.question: A row of squares made from matchsticks uses 4, 7, 10 sticks for 1, 2, 3 squares. Find the nth term and the number of sticks for 50 squares.
questions.markScheme: 1 mark: common difference 3.  1 mark: nth term 3n + 1, verified with n = 1.  1 mark: 3 × 50 + 1 = 151.

questions.question: A sequence has nth term 6n - 1. Explain why every term is odd, and why no term is a multiple of 3.
questions.answer: 6n is even so 6n - 1 is odd; 6n - 1 is one less than a multiple of 3
questions.markScheme: Strand ii-iii (Criterion B): 1 mark: 6n is always even, so 6n - 1 is odd.  1 mark: 6n = 3(2n) is a multiple of 3.  1 mark: a number one less than a multiple of 3 cannot itself be a multiple of 3.
questions.why: Testing examples shows the pattern; a justification must use the structure of 6n

tasks.title: Investigating patterns: tables in a row
tasks.context: Square tables seat 4 people. When tables are joined end to end in a row, people sit around the outside only.
steps: Draw rows of 1, 2, 3 and 4 tables and record the number of seats.
Find a general rule for the number of seats S for n tables.
Verify your rule for n = 5 by drawing.
Justify why the rule works by referring to the tables (which seats are added each time, which are lost).
Predict how many tables are needed to seat 50 people and comment on whether a row is a sensible arrangement.
tasks.model: Seats: 4, 6, 8, 10. Rule S = 2n + 2. Each new table adds 3 seats but covers 1, net +2. For 50 people, 2n + 2 ≥ 50 gives n = 24; a row of 24 tables is impractical.
tasks.bands: Level 1-2: applies a technique with help and states a pattern. Level 3-4: records data, suggests a rule (may be term-to-term). Level 5-6: correct nth-term rule, verified with a further case. Level 7-8: correct rule, verified, and justified by reference to the structure of the tables, not by checking more examples.

tasks.title: Communicating a full solution
tasks.context: Present a complete, logically organised solution to the problem below, using correct notation and showing every line of working.
steps: Make r the subject of V = πr²h.
A cylinder has volume 1500 cm³ and height 12 cm. Use your formula to find r to 1 decimal place.
Explain in one sentence why r cannot be negative in this context.
Present the whole solution so that someone who has not seen the question could follow it.
tasks.model: r = √(V ÷ (πh)). r = √(1500 ÷ (12π)) = √39.79 = 6.3 cm. A radius is a length, so the negative root is rejected.
tasks.bands: Level 1-2: some correct notation; lines of reasoning hard to follow. Level 3-4: mostly correct notation; working partly organised. Level 5-6: correct notation throughout; working organised and mostly complete; moves between formula and numbers correctly. Level 7-8: consistently correct notation; concise, complete and coherent; the rejection of the negative root is stated and justified.

tasks.title: Applying mathematics in a real-life context: choosing a phone plan
tasks.context: Plan A: 15 per month plus 0.10 per minute of calls. Plan B: 35 per month with unlimited calls. A student makes between 150 and 250 minutes of calls a month.
steps: Define a variable and write an expression for the monthly cost of each plan.
Find the number of minutes at which the two plans cost the same.
Using the student's range of 150 to 250 minutes, recommend a plan and justify it with calculations.
Comment on the degree of accuracy of your answer (what is assumed, what is rounded).
State two limitations of this model and whether your recommendation still makes sense given them.
tasks.model: m = minutes. A = 15 + 0.1m, B = 35. Equal at m = 200. At 150 minutes A = 30 (cheaper); at 250 minutes A = 40 (B cheaper). Recommendation depends on where in the range the student usually sits; a limitation is that calls are usually billed per minute rounded up, and data and texts are ignored.
tasks.bands: Level 1-2: identifies some elements; limited strategy. Level 3-4: relevant elements identified; a strategy applied with some success. Level 5-6: valid solution reached; some comment on accuracy. Level 7-8: correct solution; recommendation justified across the range; accuracy and limitations discussed and the recommendation revisited in their light.
